name: Garter Stitch Scarf
shortDescription: A quick, cozy scarf that teaches the basic single crochet stitch. Perfect for using up a skein of worsted yarn.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; no shaping, color work, or complex stitch patterns.

yarn.notes: Any smooth, medium-weight yarn works.

hook.notes: The pattern is forgiving on hook size.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for this scarf.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 20 (or any even number for desired width).
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each chain across. (19 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1 (does *not* count as a stitch), turn. Single crochet in each stitch across. (19 sc)
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue repeating Row 2 until the piece measures about 60 in (or your desired length).
**Finishing:** Fasten off, leaving a 6-inch tail. Weave in all ends with a yarn needle.
beginnerTips: Count your stitches at the end of every row to keep the edges straight.
If your edge looks wavy, you may be adding or dropping a stitch—use a stitch marker.
Keep your tension relaxed; tight stitches make the fabric stiff.
commonMistakes: Accidentally skipping the first or last stitch of a row.
Using a hook that's too small, resulting in a stiff, dense fabric.

name: Bulky Ribbed Scarf
shortDescription: A super-fast scarf using bulky yarn and simple half-double crochet. Great for beginners who want quick results.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and half-double crochet; no shaping or complex stitches.

yarn.notes: Bulky yarn makes this scarf work up very quickly.

hook.notes: A larger hook works best with bulky yarn.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 16.
**Row 1:** Half double crochet (hdc) in 3rd chain from hook and each chain across. (14 hdc), turn.
**Row 2:** Chain 2 (counts as first hdc), turn. *Half double crochet in the back loop only of each stitch across.* (14 hdc), turn.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until the scarf measures about 60 inches.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Working in the back loop only creates a ribbed texture.
Bulky yarn works up fast—great for a confidence boost.
Count your stitches each row.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to chain 2 at the start of each row.
Working through both loops instead of the back loop only.

name: Lightweight Lacy Scarf
shortDescription: A delicate, lightweight scarf using DK weight yarn. Perfect for spring or indoor wear.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and double crochet in a simple repeating pattern.

yarn.notes: A lighter weight yarn creates a drapier fabric.

hook.notes: Use a slightly smaller hook for a tighter stitch.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for a scarf.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 18.
**Row 1:** Double crochet (dc) in 4th chain from hook and each chain across. (15 dc), turn.
**Row 2:** Chain 3 (counts as first dc), turn. *Double crochet in each stitch across.* (15 dc), turn.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until scarf measures about 60 inches.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: This pattern is just one stitch repeated—perfect for muscle memory.
DK yarn is lighter; you may want a longer scarf for wrapping.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the turning chain (ch 3) counts as a stitch.

name: Color-Block Scarf
shortDescription: A simple scarf with color changes, teaching you how to switch yarn colors cleanly.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet with simple color changes.

yarn.notes: Use 2-3 contrasting colors for best effect.

**Rows 1-15:** Single crochet in each stitch across. Turn at end of each row. (19 sc per row)
**Switch to Color B:** On the last row of Color A, pull through Color B on the final yarn-over. Cut Color A, leaving a 6-inch tail.
**Rows 16-30:** Single crochet in each stitch across with Color B. Turn.
**Switch to Color C:** Repeat the color switch technique.
**Rows 31-45:** Single crochet in each stitch across with Color C.
**Continue:** Repeat color blocks until scarf measures about 60 inches.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Weave in ends as you go to avoid a pile of tails at the end.
Carry yarn up the side if stripes are narrow.
Choose contrasting colors for a bold look.
commonMistakes: Pulling the new color too tight, causing the edge to curl.
Not leaving enough tail when switching colors.

shortDescription: A small round dishcloth perfect for scrubbing dishes, worked in the round from the center out.

Pulling the center ring too tight.

name: Basic Granny Square
shortDescription: A classic granny square that introduces multiple stitch types and can be combined into larger projects.

**Seam Sides:** Slip stitch the 2 side edges together, leaving the top open.
**Handles (Row 31):** Chain 1, sc in first 10 stitches. Chain 30 (handle), skip 15 stitches, sc in next 10. Chain 30, skip 15, sc in remaining 10.
**Handle Rounds:** Work 2 more rows of sc across, working 1 sc per chain in each handle.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: The handles are worked as part of the bag, not attached separately.
Make the handles longer by chaining more.
Cotton yarn stretches—expect the bag to lengthen with use.
commonMistakes: Twisting the handle chains before working into them.
Making the handles too short to fit over the shoulder.

name: Mini Drawstring Tote
shortDescription: A tiny tote with a drawstring closure, perfect for small gifts or as a pouch.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; small size makes it quick.

yarn.notes: Scrap yarn works perfectly.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 26.
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (25 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-16:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet across. (25 sc each row)
**Drawstring Row (Row 17):** Chain 1, turn. *Sc in next 3, chain 1, skip 1.* Repeat across, ending with sc in last 3.
**Rows 18-20:** Chain 1, turn. Sc across, working 1 sc per chain-1 space. (25 sc each row)
**Seam:** Fold in half, slip stitch side edges.
**Drawstring:** Chain 50. Thread through spaces.
**Handles (optional):** Chain 20, attach to top edge on each side.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The drawstring row creates a channel for the cord.
Add handles for a tote look, or use as a simple pouch.
commonMistakes: Drawstring spaces too small or uneven.
Forgetting to weave in ends before threading.

name: Simple Crochet Bookmark
shortDescription: A quick and easy bookmark using basic stitches. Perfect for a first project or last-minute gift.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; very small project.

yarn.notes: A small amount of scrap yarn.

hook.notes: A slightly smaller hook for a denser fabric.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 6.
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (5 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-40:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet across. (5 sc each row)
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Add a tassel by cutting 6 lengths of yarn and tying them to the bottom.
beginnerTips: This project uses very little yarn—great for scraps.
Add a tassel or bead for decoration.
Keep stitches tight so the bookmark is sturdy.
commonMistakes: Making the bookmark too wide (narrow is better).
Loose tension makes the bookmark floppy.

name: Flower Bookmark
shortDescription: A charming bookmark topped with a simple crocheted flower. Great for practicing basic flower motifs.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chain, single crochet, and double crochet; the flower is a simple 5-petal motif.

yarn.notes: Use 2 colors: one for the stem, one for the flower.

instructions: **Stem:** Chain 6. Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (5 sc), turn.
**Stem Body:** Repeat rows until stem measures about 6 inches.
**Flower Center:** With flower color, chain 4, join into a ring.
**Petals:** *Chain 3, 2 double crochet (dc) into ring, chain 3, slip stitch into ring.* Repeat 4 more times for 5 petals.
**Attach:** Sew the flower to the top of the stem.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The flower is a basic 5-petal motif—easy to customize.
Add leaves by chaining 5 and working sc back down.
commonMistakes: Not securing the flower center tightly enough.
Making the stem too wide.

name: Crochet Heart Keychain
shortDescription: A cute little heart keychain that teaches simple shaping and works up in minutes.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chain, single crochet, and double crochet; introduces simple increases for shaping.

yarn.notes: Scrap yarn works perfectly.

instructions: **Center:** Chain 4, join with a slip stitch to form a ring.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), 3 dc into ring, chain 1, 4 dc into ring, chain 1, 4 dc into ring. Join with slip stitch to top of ch-3. (12 dc, 2 chain spaces)
**Finishing:** Fasten off, leaving a long tail. Sew the heart shape by pulling the tail through the center and tightening slightly.
**Attach ring:** Thread the keychain ring through the top loop.
beginnerTips: This heart is worked in one piece—no seaming required.
Use a contrasting color for the keychain ring.
Make a pair and give as a gift.
commonMistakes: Pulling the center too tight, making the heart lopsided.
Not leaving enough tail to attach the ring.

name: Star Keychain
shortDescription: A 5-pointed star keychain using simple increases and decreases. Fast and fun.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet and slip stitch; the star is created with simple increases.

yarn.notes: Scrap yarn works perfectly.

instructions: **Center Ring:** Chain 4, join with a slip stitch.
**Point 1:** Chain 5, sc in 2nd chain from hook, sc in next 3 chains. Slip stitch into the center ring.
**Point 2:** Slip stitch into center ring. Chain 5, sc in 2nd from hook, sc in next 3. Slip stitch into center.
**Points 3-5:** Repeat Point 2 three more times.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Attach keychain ring to one point.
beginnerTips: Each point is worked individually from the center ring.
Make the center ring tight to prevent gaps.
Use a star as a gift tag or bag charm.
commonMistakes: Making the center ring too loose.
Losing count of points (should be 5).

name: Simple Wristband
shortDescription: A comfortable wristband using single crochet, perfect for practicing consistent tension.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; very small and simple.

yarn.notes: Soft yarn is best for wearing on the wrist.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 8.
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (7 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-30:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet across. (7 sc each row)
**Button Loop:** Work 4 more rows on only the first 3 stitches.
**Finishing:** Sew a button to the opposite end. Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your wrist before chaining.
Add stripes by changing colors every 5 rows.
A small button is best for a comfortable closure.
commonMistakes: Making the wristband too loose or too tight.
Button loop too small for the button.

name: Braided Wristband
shortDescription: A trendy braided-look wristband made with crocheted chains braided together.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain stitches and simple braiding.

yarn.notes: Use 3 colors for a colorful braid.

instructions: **Strand 1 (Color A):** Chain 60. Fasten off.
**Strand 2 (Color B):** Chain 60. Fasten off.
**Strand 3 (Color C):** Chain 60. Fasten off.
**Braid:** Tie the 3 strands together at one end. Braid them together tightly.
**Secure:** Tie the other end to secure the braid.
**Finishing:** Sew a button to one end and a loop to the other. Or attach a clasp.
beginnerTips: Chaining is the most basic crochet skill—this is a confidence-building project.
Use colors that match your wardrobe.
Adjust chain length to fit your wrist.
commonMistakes: Chaining too tight, making the braid stiff.
Uneven tension between the 3 strands.

name: Simple Eyeglass Case
shortDescription: A padded eyeglass case using basic stitches. Great for protecting your glasses.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; simple rectangular construction with a flap.

yarn.notes: Use a soft but sturdy yarn.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 20.
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (19 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-30:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet across. (19 sc each row)
**Flap (Row 31):** Chain 1, turn. Sc in next 19 stitches, chain 6 (button loop), sc in same last stitch. Turn.
**Row 32:** Chain 1, sc across, working 6 sc into the chain-6 loop. (19 sc), turn.
**Row 33:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet across. (19 sc)
**Finishing:** Fold the case in half, slip stitch side edges. Sew button under the loop.
beginnerTips: Make the case slightly larger than your glasses.
Use a padded or thicker yarn for protection.
A flap with button closure keeps glasses secure.
commonMistakes: Making the case too tight for the glasses to slide in.
Button loop too small for the button.

name: Basic Phone Case
shortDescription: A simple pouch for your phone, with a drawstring top. Customizable to any phone size.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; simple rectangular construction.

yarn.notes: A soft but durable yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is important for a snug phone fit.

instructions: **Measure Your Phone:** Chain should be 2 inches wider than your phone width.
**Foundation Chain:** Chain to match your phone width (plus 2 inches).
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain and each across. Turn.
**Rows 2-30:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet across until piece measures 1.5x your phone height.
**Drawstring Holes:** Sc in first 3 stitches, *chain 1, skip 1, sc in next 3.* Repeat across.
**Next Row:** Sc across, working 1 sc per chain-1 space.
**Fold & Seam:** Fold in half, slip stitch side edges.
**Drawstring:** Chain 40. Thread through holes.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your phone before chaining for a custom fit.
Use a soft yarn to avoid scratching the phone.
The drawstring keeps the phone secure.
commonMistakes: Making the case too tight for the phone.
Forgetting to leave space for the drawstring channel.

name: Water Bottle Holder
shortDescription: A sling for your water bottle with an adjustable strap. Perfect for hikes or daily walks.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet; simple cylinder construction.

yarn.notes: Cotton is sturdy and washable.

instructions: **Measure Bottle:** Chain should fit around the bottle snugly.
**Foundation Chain:** Chain to match bottle circumference.
**Row 1:** Join with a slip stitch to form a ring. Chain 1, single crochet (sc) in each chain around. Join. (sc count = chain count)
**Rounds 2-20:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Join. Continue until holder covers the bottle body.
**Strap (Row 21):** Chain 1, sc in next 8 stitches. Chain 60 (strap). Skip 20 stitches, sc in last 8.
**Strap Reinforcement:** Work 2 more rows of sc around the entire top edge, including the strap.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The holder should be snug but not tight on the bottle.
Adjust strap length for shoulder or hand carry.
Cotton yarn is best for durability on the go.
commonMistakes: Making the holder too loose, causing the bottle to slip out.
Twisting the chain when joining the ring.

name: Slouchy Beanie
shortDescription: A relaxed beanie worked in the round with a ribbed brim and simple crown decreases.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires working in the round, maintaining stitch count, and making evenly spaced decreases for the crown.

yarn.notes: Wool blends have good elasticity for hats.

instructions: **Brim:** Chain 11 loosely.
**Row 1:** Single crochet (sc) in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (10 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-40:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in back loop only of each stitch. (10 sc each row)
**Join Brim:** Fold to form a ring. Slip stitch short ends together.
**Body Rnd 1:** Chain 1, work 60 sc evenly around the brim edge. Join. (60 sc)
**Body Rnds 2-10:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Join. (60 sc)
**Crown Dec Rnd 11:** Chain 1, *sc in next 8 stitches, sc2tog.* Repeat around. Join. (54)
**Rnds 12-15:** Continue decreasing: sc in 7 then sc2tog, sc in 6 then sc2tog, etc. Join each round.
**Finishing:** Cut tail, thread through remaining stitches, pull tight. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to mark the start of each round.
sc2tog: insert hook, yo, pull up loop (2 loops), insert hook in next stitch, yo, pull up loop (3 loops), yo, pull through all 3 loops.
Try the hat on as you go to check fit.
commonMistakes: Losing count between decreases causing an uneven crown.
Brim too tight; chain loosely.

name: Fingerless Gloves
shortDescription: Cozy fingerless gloves with a thumb opening, working flat with seaming.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires shaping for the thumb hole, working flat and seaming, and maintaining consistent tension.

yarn.notes: A soft, warm yarn works best.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 28 (adjust for wrist circumference).
**Ribbing:** Chain 9. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (8 sc), turn.
**Ribbing Rows:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in back loop only across. Repeat until piece fits wrist. Join ends.
**Body Rnd 1:** Chain 1, work 40 sc evenly around ribbing edge. Join. (40 sc)
**Body Rnds 2-5:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Join.
**Thumb Hole Rnd 6:** Chain 1, sc in next 15 stitches, chain 5, skip 5 stitches, sc in remaining 20. Join.
**Body Rnds 7-10:** Chain 1, sc around, working 5 sc into the chain-5 space. Join.
**Top Edging:** Chain 1, *sc in next, hdc in next, dc in next.* Repeat. Join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Repeat for second glove.
beginnerTips: Work the second glove identically to the first.
Adjust the thumb hole position by changing where you start the chain-5.
The hdc/dc edging prevents the top from curling.
commonMistakes: Making the thumb hole too small.
Uneven stitch count between the two gloves.

name: Mesh Market Bag
shortDescription: A stretchy mesh bag worked in the round with a drawstring closure and sturdy handles.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires working in the round, chain spaces, mesh stitch pattern, and attaching handles.

yarn.notes: Cotton is strong and washable for market bags.

gauge.notes: Gauge not critical for this bag.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, join with slip stitch to form ring.
**Rnd 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), 11 dc into ring. Join. (12 dc)
**Rnd 2:** Chain 3, 2 dc in each stitch. Join. (24 dc)
**Rnd 3:** Chain 3, *dc in next, 2 dc in next.* Repeat. Join. (36 dc)
**Rnd 4:** Chain 3, *dc in next 2, 2 dc in next.* Repeat. Join. (48 dc)
**Mesh Body:** Chain 1, *sc in next, chain 3, skip 2 stitches.* Repeat around. Join.
**Repeat Mesh:** Continue mesh rounds until bag measures ~12 inches tall.
**Handle Openings:** Chain 1, *sc in next, chain 30 (handle), skip 10 stitches, sc in next.* Repeat twice. Join.
**Handle Reinforcement:** Sc around each handle, work 2 sc in each chain. Join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The mesh stretches significantly when loaded.
Make the base wider for a roomier bag.
Cotton yarn is preferred for strength and washability.
commonMistakes: Base too small causing the bag to be narrow.
Skipping the wrong number of stitches in mesh pattern.

name: Chevron Lap Blanket
shortDescription: A warm lap blanket with a chevron ripple pattern using increases and decreases.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires maintaining a repeating pattern of increases and decreases, consistent tension, and reading a stitch pattern.

yarn.notes: Acrylic is lightweight and washable for blankets.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 104 (multiple of 16 + 8).
**Row 1:** Dc in 4th chain from hook. *Dc in next 6, (dc, ch 1, dc) in next, dc in next 7, skip 2.* Repeat across. Turn.
**Row 2:** Chain 3 (counts as dc). *Dc in next 6, (dc, ch 1, dc) in next, dc in next 7, skip 2.* Repeat across. Turn.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until piece measures ~40 inches long.
**Border Rnd 1:** Sc evenly around all 4 edges, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Border Rnd 2:** *Sc in next, chain 3, skip 1.* Repeat around. Join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Use stitch markers at the peak (ch-1 space) and valley (skip 2) to stay on track.
Count your stitches each row—each peak and valley should line up.
Change colors every few rows for a striped effect.
commonMistakes: Losing the peak or valley position, throwing off the chevron pattern.
Forgetting the turning chain counts as the first dc.

name: Cable-Look Scarf
shortDescription: A knit-look scarf with braided cable effects created using front-post and back-post double crochet.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires front-post and back-post double crochet stitches, following a cable pattern repeat, and maintaining consistent tension.

yarn.notes: Smooth yarn shows stitch definition best.

gauge.notes: Gauge not critical for a scarf.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 22.
**Row 1:** Dc in 4th chain and each across. (19 dc), turn.
**Row 2 (Setup):** Chain 3, *fpdc around next 2, bpdc around next 2.* Repeat across. Turn.
**Cable Row 3:** Chain 3, skip next 2 fpdc, fpdc around next 2, then fpdc around the 2 skipped stitches (cross). Bpdc around next 2. Repeat cable cross across. Turn.
**Row 4:** Chain 3, *fpdc around fpdc, bpdc around bpdc.* Repeat across. Turn.
**Repeat Rows 3-4:** Continue until scarf measures ~60 inches.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Block lightly to open the cable pattern.
beginnerTips: fpdc: yarn over, insert hook from front to back around the post, complete as dc.
The cable cross is created by working out of order—stitch into the farther post first.
Blocking helps the cable pattern open up and look professional.
commonMistakes: Confusing fpdc and bpdc placement.
Skipping the turning chain at the start of each row.

name: Triangle Lace Shawl
shortDescription: A lightweight lace shawl worked from the top down with increasing rows and open shells.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires tracking increases on both edges, working lace shells, and reading a stitch pattern.

yarn.notes: Lightweight yarn creates a drapey shawl.

gauge.notes: Gauge is forgiving for a shawl.

instructions: **Center Top:** Chain 4, join to form ring.
**Row 1:** Chain 4 (counts as dc + ch 1), (dc, ch 1) 3 times into ring, dc. Turn. (5 dc, 4 ch-1 spaces)
**Row 2:** Chain 4, dc in same stitch. *Ch 1, dc in next dc* across. In last dc: dc, ch 1, dc. Turn.
**Shell Row 3:** Chain 3, 3 dc in same. *Skip 1, 3 dc in next dc* across. In last: 4 dc. Turn.
**Increase Row 4:** Chain 4, dc in same. *Ch 1, skip 1, dc in next dc* across. In last: dc, ch 1, dc. Turn.
**Repeat Shell & Increase Rows:** Alternate rows 3-4 until shawl reaches desired width.
**Border:** Sc evenly around all 3 edges. *Ch 3, skip 1, sc* for picot edge.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, block to open the lace pattern.
beginnerTips: Place stitch markers at the center top to track the midline.
Blocking is essential for lace—it opens the stitch pattern dramatically.
Use a larger hook for a drapier fabric.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the increases on both edges, causing a straight edge.
Not blocking the finished shawl.

name: Structured Bucket Hat
shortDescription: A firm bucket hat with a wide brim, worked in continuous rounds with even increases.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires working in continuous (spiral) rounds, precise increase spacing, and consistent tension for a structured fabric.

yarn.notes: Cotton holds shape better than acrylic for structured hats.

hook.notes: Slightly smaller hook for firm fabric.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines hat fit and brim size.

instructions: **Crown:** Make a magic ring. Rnd 1: 6 sc into ring. (6 sc)
**Rnd 2:** 2 sc in each stitch. (12 sc)
**Rnd 3:** *Sc in next, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. (18 sc)
**Rnd 4:** *Sc in next 2, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. (24 sc)
**Rnds 5-8:** Continue increasing: sc in 3 then inc, sc in 4 then inc, etc. (48 sc)
**Rnds 9-16 (Sides):** Sc in each stitch (no increases). (48 sc each)
**Brim Rnd 17:** *Sc in next 5, 2 sc in next.* Repeat.
**Brim Rnds 18-20:** Continue increasing each round (sc in 6 then inc, sc in 7 then inc).
**Brim Edge:** Slip stitch in each stitch around for a clean edge.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker in the first stitch of each round—continuous rounds have no visible join.
Crown increases create a flat circle; stop when it fits your head.
The brim should be firm enough to hold its shape.
commonMistakes: Not marking the first stitch in spiral rounds.
Loose tension makes the brim floppy.

name: Baby Booties
shortDescription: Adorable crochet booties for babies with a simple sole, sides, and ankle ties.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires working in the round, shaping the toe and heel, working into front loops only, and seaming.

yarn.notes: Soft, washable yarn is best for baby items.

hook.notes: Smaller hook for a firm fabric.

gauge.notes: Gauge is critical for correct shoe size.

instructions: **Sole:** Chain 8.
**Rnd 1:** Sc in 2nd chain and next 5 chains, 3 sc in last chain. Other side: sc in next 5, 2 sc in last. Join. (16 sc)
**Rnd 2:** Ch 1, 2 sc in first, sc in next 5, 2 sc in next 3, sc in next 5, 2 sc in next 2. Join. (22 sc)
**Sides:** Working in front loop only: Ch 1, sc in each stitch around. Join. (22 sc)
**Rnds 4-6:** Ch 1, sc in each stitch around. Join.
**Toe Decrease:** Fold bootie flat. Sc across top half only (11 stitches), sc2tog at center. Turn.
**Ankle:** Ch 1, sc around the top opening for 4 rounds.
**Ties:** Chain 40. Thread through ankle rounds, tie in a bow.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Repeat for second bootie.
beginnerTips: Keep both booties identical by counting rows carefully.
Working in front loop only creates a defined edge between sole and sides.
Add ribbon instead of crochet ties for a polished look.
commonMistakes: Making the sole too small or too large for the intended baby size.
Uneven stitch count between the two booties.

name: Corner-to-Corner Square
shortDescription: A square worked diagonally using the corner-to-corner technique with increasing and decreasing blocks.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires understanding diagonal construction, block counting, and decreasing on both edges.

yarn.notes: Multiple colors work well for graphghans.

gauge.notes: Each pixel is a block of 3 dc.

instructions: **Block 1:** Chain 6. Dc in 4th, 5th, and 6th chain from hook. (1 block)
**Row 2 (Increase):** Chain 6. Dc in 4th, 5th, 6th chains. Sl st to ch-3 space of previous block. Ch 3, 3 dc in same space. (2 blocks)
**Row 3:** Chain 6, dc in 4th-6th. Sl st to next block's ch-3 space, ch 3, 3 dc. Repeat. (3 blocks)
**Continue Increasing:** Add one block each row until the square reaches desired width.
**Decrease Row:** Sl st across first block. Ch 3, 3 dc in next ch-3 space. Continue across. (1 fewer block)
**Continue Decreasing:** Decrease each row until 1 block remains.
**Final Block:** Sl st across, ch 3, 3 dc, fasten off.
**Border:** Sc evenly around the square, 3 sc in each corner.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Each C2C block = chain 3 + 3 double crochet (into the chain-3 space).
Use a graph or chart for color changes.
Carry unused yarn across the back for small color blocks.
commonMistakes: Counting blocks incorrectly—use a row counter.
Pulling the slip stitch join too tight, puckering the fabric.

name: Amigurumi Ball
shortDescription: A perfect round ball using continuous spiral rounds with even increases and decreases—the foundation of amigurumi.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires working in continuous (spiral) rounds, tracking increases and decreases precisely, and invisible finishing.

yarn.notes: Smooth yarn shows stitch definition best.

hook.notes: Smaller hook for tight stitches (prevents stuffing from showing).

gauge.notes: Tight gauge is important to hide stuffing.

instructions: **Rnd 1:** Make a magic ring, 6 sc into ring. (6 sc)
**Rnd 2:** 2 sc in each stitch. (12 sc)
**Rnd 3:** *Sc in next, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. (18 sc)
**Rnd 4:** *Sc in next 2, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. (24 sc)
**Rnd 5:** *Sc in next 3, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. (30 sc)
**Rnds 6-10:** Sc in each stitch. (30 sc each)
**Rnd 11:** *Sc in next 3, sc2tog.* Repeat. (24 sc)
**Rnd 12:** *Sc in next 2, sc2tog.* Repeat. (18 sc)
**Rnd 13:** *Sc in next, sc2tog.* Repeat. (12 sc)
**Stuff firmly before closing.**
**Rnd 14:** sc2tog around. (6 sc)
**Finishing:** Cut tail, thread through front loops of remaining 6 stitches, pull tight. Weave in end.
beginnerTips: Always use a stitch marker for spiral rounds—there's no join to reset your count.
Stuff firmly but not bulging; shape as you stuff.
The magic ring creates a closed center with no hole.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to mark the first stitch of each round.
Stitches too loose—stuffing will peek through.

name: Granny Hexagon Throw
shortDescription: A hexagonal granny motif that can be joined to make a blanket, shawl, or cardigan.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires working hexagon increases (6 corners), joining motifs, and maintaining consistent tension across multiples.

yarn.notes: Per hexagon; adjust for total desired.

instructions: **Rnd 1:** Chain 4, join to form ring. Ch 3 (counts as dc), dc into ring, *ch 2, 2 dc into ring.* Repeat 4 times, ch 2, join. (6 dc pairs, 6 ch-2 spaces)
**Rnd 2:** Sl st to first ch-2 space. (Ch 3, dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in same. *Ch 1, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in next.* Repeat 4 times, ch 1, join.
**Rnd 3:** Sl st to first corner. (Ch 3, dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in corner. *Ch 1, 2 dc in ch-1 space, ch 1, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in corner.* Repeat.
**Rnd 4:** Continue same pattern: corners get (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc), sides get 2 dc in each ch-1 space.
**Repeat Rnd 4** until hexagon reaches desired size.
**Joining:** To join, replace corner ch-2 with ch 1, sl st to adjacent motif corner, ch 1.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block all motifs to same size before joining.
beginnerTips: Each corner has 2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc. Each side space gets ch 1, 2 dc.
Make several hexagons and join for a throw or cardigan.
Blocking makes joining much easier—all motifs should be identical.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the chain-1 between side clusters.
Hexagon not lying flat—check corner increases.

name: Mandala Wall Hanging
shortDescription: A colorful mandala with concentric rounds of different stitch patterns, finished with a hanging loop.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires combining multiple stitch types (sc, hdc, dc, tr, picot), tracking complex round patterns, and color changes.

yarn.notes: Multiple colors make the mandala pop—use 3-5 colors.

hook.notes: Slightly smaller hook for firm fabric.

gauge.notes: Gauge not critical for wall hanging.

instructions: **Center Rnd 1 (Color A):** Chain 6, join. Ch 3, 11 dc into ring. Join. (12 dc)
**Rnd 2 (Color A):** Ch 1, *sc in next, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. Join. (18 sc)
**Rnd 3 (Color B):** Join new color. Ch 1, *sc in next 2, 2 sc in next.* Repeat. Join. (24 sc)
**Rnd 4 (Color B):** Ch 1, *hdc in next 2, dc in next, tr in next, ch 2, tr in next, dc in next, hdc in next 2.* Repeat to form 4 petals. Join.
**Rnd 5 (Color C):** Join new color. Ch 1, sc in each stitch, 2 sc in each ch-2 corner. (36 sc)
**Rnd 6 (Color C):** Ch 1, *sc in next 3, ch 3, skip 1, sc in next 3.* Repeat. Join.
**Rnd 7 (Color D):** Join new color. Ch 1, *sc in next 2, 3 dc in ch-3 space, sc in next 2.* Repeat. Join.
**Rnd 8 (Color D):** Ch 1, sc in each stitch, sc in each ch-1 space between dc groups. (60 sc)
**Rnd 9 (Color E):** Join new color. *Sc in next 4, ch 5, skip 2.* Repeat. Join.
**Rnd 10 (Color E):** *In each ch-5: sc, hdc, 3 dc, hdc, sc.* Sl st between petals. Repeat.
**Hanging Loop:** Ch 20, slip stitch to starting point.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Block to open the stitch patterns.
beginnerTips: Change colors by pulling the new yarn through the last yarn-over of the previous stitch.
Blocking transforms a mandala—it opens the lace and evens the stitches.
Mount on a wooden dowel or embroidery hoop for display.
commonMistakes: Pulling color changes too tight, puckering the fabric.
Skipping the slip stitch join at the end of each round.

name: Quilted Eyeglass Case
shortDescription: A padded eyeglass case using the thermal stitch (back-loop only) for a quilted look. Keeps lenses safe and scratch-free.

difficulty.reasoning: Works in the back loop only, which is a simple variation of single crochet.

yarn.notes: Cotton gives nice stitch definition.

hook.notes: A slightly smaller hook creates a denser fabric.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 16.
**Row 1:** Single crochet in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (15 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet in back loop only of each stitch across. (15 sc)
**Repeat:** Repeat Row 2 until piece measures 7 inches tall.
**Fold and seam:** Fold in half widthwise. Single crochet through both layers along the bottom and side edges.
**Optional flap:** Chain 10 from the top back edge, slip stitch to front, fasten off.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Sew on button if desired.
beginnerTips: Count stitches each row to keep the rectangle even.
Block the finished piece to flatten the seam.
commonMistakes: Working through both loops instead of the back loop.
Skipping the turning chain.

name: Textured Phone Sleeve
shortDescription: A simple phone sleeve using half double crochet. Works up fast and makes a great gift.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and half double crochet with simple seaming.

yarn.notes: Cotton is durable and washable.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 16 (or width to fit your phone).
**Row 1:** Half double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (14 hdc)
**Row 2:** Chain 2 (counts as first hdc), turn. Half double crochet in each stitch across. (14 hdc)
**Repeat:** Repeat Row 2 until piece is twice the height of your phone.
**Fold and seam:** Fold in half. Slip stitch or single crochet along the bottom and one side edge.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Turn right side out.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to keep track of the first and last stitch.
Make the sleeve slightly snug — cotton stretches a bit with use.
commonMistakes: Skipping the first stitch after the turning chain.
Making the sleeve too tight — leave a little room.

name: Simple Bottle Bag
shortDescription: A sturdy mesh bag to carry a water bottle. Uses double crochet mesh for stretch and breathability.

difficulty.reasoning: Introduces working in the round and basic mesh pattern (chain-space).

yarn.notes: Cotton holds shape well and is washable.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, join with slip stitch to form a ring.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), work 11 double crochet into ring, join. (12 dc)
**Round 2:** Chain 3, double crochet in same stitch, 2 dc in each stitch around, join. (24 dc)
**Round 3:** Chain 4 (counts as dc + ch 1), skip 1 stitch, dc in next stitch, chain 1, skip 1 — repeat around, join.
**Round 4:** Slip stitch to chain-1 space, chain 4 (counts as dc + ch 1), dc in next chain-1 space, chain 1 — repeat around, join.
**Repeat Round 4:** Continue until bag measures about 8 inches tall.
**Handle:** Chain 30, skip 6 mesh spaces, slip stitch into next space, chain 30, skip 6, join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off and weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Place a stitch marker at the start of each round.
The mesh pattern is very forgiving — just keep the chain-1 spaces lined up.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the chain 1 between double crochets.
Losing count of skipped stitches in the handle round.

name: Simple Headband
shortDescription: A twisted knot headband made with half double crochet. Quick, stylish, and uses very little yarn.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple rectangle seamed with a twist. Only chain and hdc needed.

yarn.notes: Any soft worsted weight yarn.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 14.
**Row 1:** Half double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (12 hdc)
**Row 2:** Chain 2 (counts as first hdc), turn. Half double crochet in each stitch across. (12 hdc)
**Repeat:** Repeat Row 2 until piece measures 18-20 inches long.
**Twist and seam:** Bring both short ends together. Twist one end 180 degrees, then slip stitch or sew the ends together.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. The twist creates a stylish knot at the center front.
beginnerTips: Block the band if it curls at the edges.
Make it longer for a looser fit, shorter for a tighter fit.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to twist before seaming.
Making the band too short — measure around your head first.

name: Granny Square Tote
shortDescription: A cheerful tote bag made from joined granny squares. A perfect next step after learning the granny square.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires making multiple granny squares and joining them, plus adding handles.

yarn.notes: Cotton is best for structure. Use 2-3 colors for visual interest.

gauge.notes: Check that each square is the same size.

instructions: **Make 6 granny squares (4 inches each):** Use the pattern from the Granny Square category.
**Arrange:** Lay out 2 rows of 3 squares each.
**Join rows:** Using a whip stitch or single crochet join, attach squares side by side in each row.
**Join rows together:** Seam the two rows together to form a 2x3 rectangle.
**Fold:** Fold the rectangle in half widthwise — the bottom row becomes the front and back panels.
**Seam sides:** Single crochet or whip stitch the side edges together.
**Handles:** Chain 60. Attach with slip stitch at the top edge of each side panel. Repeat for second handle.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends. Line with fabric if desired.
beginnerTips: Block all squares to the same size before joining.
Use a contrasting color for the join to make it decorative.
commonMistakes: Squares not matching in size — always block them.
Twisting the handles when attaching.

name: Corner-to-Corner Baby Blanket
shortDescription: A modern corner-to-corner (C2C) baby blanket using double crochet. Works up diagonally, making it easy to resize.

difficulty.reasoning: Introduces increasing and decreasing (diagonal work), but uses only double crochet and chains.

yarn.notes: Soft washable yarn is best for baby items.

hook.notes: Slightly larger hook gives nice drape.

gauge.notes: Work a test square to check.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 6.
**Block 1:** Double crochet in 4th chain from hook and next 2 chains. (1 tile made)
**Row 2 (increase):** Chain 6, dc in 4th ch and next 2 ch. Sl st to chain-3 space of previous tile. Chain 3, work 3 dc in same space.
**Continue increasing:** Follow C2C method, adding one tile per row until the blanket reaches half the desired size.
**Decrease:** At the start of the decrease rows, slip stitch across the first tile, chain 3, work 3 dc in next space. Continue across.
**Finish:** When the blanket is square, fasten off.
**Border (optional):** Single crochet evenly around all edges, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends. Block gently.
beginnerTips: Use a different color for each row to see the diagonal structure clearly.
C2C is very forgiving — missed stitches are easy to fix.
commonMistakes: Losing count of tiles in the increase section.
Skipping the chain 3 at the start of a new tile.

name: Simple Triangle Shawl
shortDescription: A top-down triangle shawl using double crochet. Easy to resize and perfect for using one beautiful skein.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple increases (dc clusters) at the center and edges. No stitch pattern changes.

yarn.notes: A soft, drapey yarn works best. Variegated yarn creates a beautiful gradient effect.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 4, join with slip stitch to form a ring.
**Row 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), work 3 dc in ring, chain 2, 4 dc in ring. Turn. (8 dc, 1 ch-2 space)
**Row 2:** Chain 3, 3 dc in same stitch, dc in next 3 stitches, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in corner space, dc in next 3 stitches, 4 dc in last stitch. Turn.
**Row 3:** Chain 3, 3 dc in same stitch, dc across to corner, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in corner, dc across, 4 dc in last stitch. Turn.
**Repeat Row 3:** Continue until shawl reaches desired size. Each row adds 6 dc total.
**Border (optional):** Single crochet around all edges with 3 sc in the corner.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Block to open up the stitches.
beginnerTips: Place stitch markers at the corner space so you never miss the increase.
The shawl grows fast — each row only adds a few minutes.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to turn at the end of each row.
Working too tightly — a loose tension gives better drape.

name: Newborn Hat
shortDescription: A simple newborn hat worked in the round. Uses double crochet and works up in under an hour.

difficulty.reasoning: Worked in the round with simple increases. Uses only chain and double crochet.

yarn.notes: Use a soft, washable yarn labeled for babies.

hook.notes: Standard hook for light weight yarn.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 4, join with slip stitch.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), 11 double crochet into ring, join. (12 dc)
**Round 2:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, 2 dc in each stitch around, join. (24 dc)
**Round 3:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, dc in next, (2 dc in next, dc in next) repeat around, join. (36 dc)
**Round 4:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, dc in next 2, (2 dc in next, dc in next 2) repeat around, join. (48 dc)
**Rounds 5-8:** Chain 3, dc in each stitch around, join. (48 dc each round)
**Finishing:** Fasten off. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track the start of each round.
Add a pom-pom on top for cuteness.
commonMistakes: Increasing too many or too few stitches — count after each round.
Not joining at the end of each round.

name: Crochet Cube (Amigurumi)
shortDescription: A soft, squishy crochet cube made from 6 squares sewn together. A perfect first amigurumi project.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires making 6 squares and seaming them together. Basic shaping through seaming rather than increases/decreases.

yarn.notes: Two contrasting colors make it more fun!

instructions: **Make 6 squares (same size):** Chain 11. Single crochet in 2nd ch from hook and each across. (10 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet in each stitch across. (10 sc)
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until square (10 rows total). Fasten off.
**Repeat for 5 more squares.**
**Arrange:** Lay out the 6 squares in a cross shape (like a T) — 4 in a row, 1 above the 2nd, 1 below the 2nd.
**Seam:** Using whip stitch or single crochet join, seam the edges together to form a cube.
**Stuff:** Before closing the last side, fill the cube with stuffing.
**Close:** Seam the final edge. Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Make all squares the same tension for a perfect cube.
Squeeze the stuffing into the corners before closing.
commonMistakes: Squares not matching size — check your gauge.
Overstuffing — it should be firm but squishy.

name: Potholder (Double Thick)
shortDescription: A double-thick cotton potholder worked as two layers joined at the edge. Uses single crochet throughout.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple single crochet rectangle; joining two layers adds a practical skill.

yarn.notes: Must use 100% cotton — acrylic melts under heat!

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 26.
**Row 1:** Single crochet in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (25 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Single crochet in each stitch across. (25 sc)
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue for 25 rows total to form a square.
**Fasten off.** Make a second identical square.
**Join:** Place the two squares together. Single crochet through both layers around all 4 edges, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Hanging loop:** At one corner, chain 12, slip stitch back to same stitch to form a loop.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Always use 100% cotton for potholders — acrylic can melt!
Block both squares to the same size before joining.
commonMistakes: Using acrylic yarn (unsafe for heat).
The two squares not matching size.

name: Scrunchie
shortDescription: A quick and stylish hair scrunchie using single crochet. Uses scraps of yarn and a hair elastic.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple single crochet around an elastic. Quick and forgiving.

yarn.notes: Great for scrap yarn! Any weight works.

instructions: **Setup:** Hold the hair elastic as your foundation ring.
**Round 1:** Insert hook through the elastic, yarn over, pull up a loop. Single crochet around the elastic, covering it completely. Work as many sc as needed to fill it (usually 30-40).
**Join:** Slip stitch to first sc.
**Round 2:** Chain 1, 2 single crochet in each stitch around, join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, leaving a tail. Sew the end into the scrunchie to hide. Fluff and shape.
beginnerTips: Use stretchy cotton for better hold.
White elastic shows through thin yarn — darker yarns hide it better.
commonMistakes: Working too tightly — the elastic needs room to stretch.
Not covering the elastic completely in the first round.

name: Baby Rattle
shortDescription: A safe and soft baby rattle with a crochet ball and a bell inside. A charming baby shower gift.

difficulty.reasoning: Working in the round with increases and decreases to form a ball.

yarn.notes: Use a soft, washable yarn. Avoid fuzzy yarns that shed.

hook.notes: Slightly smaller hook for tight fabric.

notions: Small jingle bell or rattle insert

instructions: **Round 1:** Make a magic ring, work 6 sc into ring. (6 sc)
**Round 2:** 2 sc in each stitch around. (12 sc)
**Round 3:** (Sc in next stitch, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (18 sc)
**Round 4:** (Sc in next 2, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (24 sc)
**Rounds 5-7:** Sc in each stitch around. (24 sc each)
**Round 8:** (Sc in next 2, sc2tog) repeat around. (18 sc)
**Round 9:** (Sc in next, sc2tog) repeat around. (12 sc)
**Insert bell and stuff:** Place the bell inside, then stuff firmly.
**Round 10:** Sc2tog around until closed. (6 sc)
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in the end.
beginnerTips: Use a tight tension so stuffing doesn't show through.
Make sure the bell is securely enclosed.
commonMistakes: Stitches too loose — stuffing shows through.
Forgetting to insert the bell before closing.

name: Drawstring Pouch
shortDescription: A simple drawstring pouch worked in the round. Great for gifts, jewelry, or small items.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple tube worked in the round with a drawstring cord. Basic sc and chains.

yarn.notes: Cotton gives nice structure.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 26, join with slip stitch.
**Round 1:** Chain 1, sc in each chain around, join. (26 sc)
**Rounds 2-12:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around, join.
**Eyelet round:** Chain 4 (counts as dc + ch 1), skip 1 stitch, dc in next, ch 1, skip 1 — repeat around, join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off.
**Drawstring:** Chain 60. Weave through the eyelet holes. Tie knots at the ends.
beginnerTips: Block the pouch to flatten the bottom curve.
Use a contrasting color for the drawstring.
commonMistakes: Eyelet holes not lining up — count the stitches between each ch-1.
Drawstring too short — make it generous.

name: Solid Granny Throw
shortDescription: A solid (no holes) granny square blanket using double crochet. Dense and warm — classic stashbuster.

difficulty.reasoning: Solid granny square with ch-2 corners. Repetitive and meditative.

yarn.notes: Great for using up scrap yarn in stripes.

hook.notes: Slightly larger hook for better drape.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 4, join with slip stitch.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), 2 dc in ring, ch 2, (3 dc in ring, ch 2) 3 times, join. (12 dc, 4 ch-2 spaces)
**Round 2:** Slip stitch to corner space. Chain 3, 2 dc in space, ch 2, 3 dc in same space. (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in each corner space around, join.
**Round 3:** Slip stitch to corner. Chain 3, 2 dc in corner, ch 2, 3 dc in same corner. Dc in each dc across side to next corner. Repeat for each side, join.
**Repeat Round 3:** Continue until blanket reaches desired size. Add more rows for a larger blanket.
**Border (optional):** Single crochet evenly around all edges.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Change colors every few rounds for a striped effect.
The ch-2 corners are the only tricky part — place markers there.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to chain 2 at the corners.
Working extra stitches into the corners.

name: Rectangle Poncho
shortDescription: A simple poncho made from two rectangles sewn together. Cozy, stylish, and very beginner-friendly.

difficulty.reasoning: Just two rectangles with basic seaming.

yarn.notes: Soft, drapable yarn works best.

hook.notes: Larger hook for a looser fabric.

instructions: **Make two rectangles (same size):** Chain 40 (or desired width).
**Row 1:** Half double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (38 hdc)
**Row 2:** Chain 2, turn. Hdc in each stitch across.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until rectangle measures about 20 inches long.
**Repeat for second rectangle.**
**Sew shoulder seams:** Fold each rectangle in half. Sew the top edges of one rectangle to the top edges of the other, leaving a gap in the center for the neck opening (about 8 inches).
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Add fringe if desired.
beginnerTips: Block the rectangles before seaming for a cleaner finish.
Make the neck opening generous — it's hard to fix later.
commonMistakes: Making the neck opening too small.
Not matching stitch counts on both rectangles.

name: Amigurumi Egg
shortDescription: A cute, simple amigurumi egg shape. Works up in minutes — perfect for Easter or learning amigurumi basics.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple increases and decreases in the round. Very small project.

yarn.notes: Scrap yarn works great.

instructions: **Round 1:** Magic ring, 6 sc in ring. (6)
**Round 2:** 2 sc in each stitch. (12)
**Round 3:** (Sc in next, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (18)
**Round 4:** (Sc in next 2, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (24)
**Rounds 5-7:** Sc in each stitch around. (24)
**Round 8:** (Sc in next 2, sc2tog) repeat around. (18)
**Round 9:** (Sc in next, sc2tog) repeat around. (12)
**Stuff firmly.**
**Round 10:** Sc2tog around. (6)
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in the end.
beginnerTips: Use a tight tension so stuffing doesn't peek through.
Vary colors for a whole set of decorated eggs.
commonMistakes: Not stuffing firmly enough — eggs should be solid.
Loose tension causing gaps.

name: Simple Throw Pillow Cover
shortDescription: A 16-inch square pillow cover using half double crochet. Uses a simple envelope closure on the back.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple rectangle worked flat. Envelope back uses basic seaming.

yarn.notes: Cotton holds shape best.
