**Row 2:** Chain 2, turn. Hdc in each stitch across.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until panel is 16 inches tall.
**Make back panels (2 pieces):** Make 2 panels the same width (chain 50, hdc in 3rd chain and each across, 48 hdc each row) — each 11 inches tall (about 15 rows).
**Button band (left back panel):** Sc evenly along one long edge. Next row: sc in 3, ch 2, skip 2, *sc in 14, ch 2, skip 2; repeat from * once more, sc in last 3. (3 buttonholes)
**Sew buttons** on right back panel edge opposite each buttonhole. Overlap panels with button band on top.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Insert pillow form.
beginnerTips: Block the panels before seaming for a professional look.
Use a pillow insert that's 1-2 inches larger for a snug fit.
commonMistakes: Panels not matching size — block them.
Buttonholes too small — make them generous.

name: Slouchy Beret
shortDescription: A slouchy beret-style hat worked top-down. Uses double crochet increases for a relaxed, stylish fit.

difficulty.reasoning: Top-down increases, then even rounds. Uses dc and basic shaping.

yarn.notes: A soft, drapey yarn works best.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 4, join with slip stitch.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), 11 dc in ring, join. (12 dc)
**Round 2:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, 2 dc in each stitch around, join. (24 dc)
**Round 3:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, dc in next, (2 dc in next, dc in next) repeat around, join. (36 dc)
**Round 4:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, dc in next 2, (2 dc in next, dc in next 2) repeat, join. (48 dc)
**Round 5:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, dc in next 3, (2 dc in next, dc in next 3) repeat, join. (60 dc)
**Round 6:** Chain 3, dc in same stitch, dc in next 4, (2 dc in next, dc in next 4) repeat, join. (72 dc)
**Rounds 7-12:** Chain 3, dc in each stitch around, join. (72 dc each)
**Ribbed brim:** Ch 1, sc in each stitch around for 4 rounds.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Adjust the slouch by adding or removing even rounds.
A looser gauge gives more drape and slouch.
commonMistakes: Making the crown too large — stop increasing when it's palm-sized.
Brim too tight — use a smaller hook for the brim if needed.

name: Moss Stitch Scarf
shortDescription: A textured scarf using the moss stitch (alternating sc and ch-1). A great next step after basic stitches.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple 2-row repeat with chain spaces. Easy to learn and memorize.

yarn.notes: Solid or semi-solid colors show the texture best.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain an even number (e.g., 24).
**Row 1:** Sc in 2nd chain from hook, chain 1, skip 1 — repeat across, ending with sc in last chain.
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in first sc, *sc in next chain-1 space, chain 1, skip next sc; repeat from * to end, ending with sc in last chain-1 space, sc in last sc.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue until scarf reaches desired length (about 60 inches).
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The moss stitch is also called the woven or linen stitch.
It looks different on each side — pick your favorite as the right side.
commonMistakes: Working into the wrong spaces — only work sc into chain-1 spaces.
Losing count of the pattern repeat.

name: Infinity Scarf (Mobius)
shortDescription: A twisted infinity scarf worked in the round. A simple twist gives a modern look.

difficulty.reasoning: Worked in the round with a twist. Uses only half double crochet.

yarn.notes: Variegated yarn looks great.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 100. Join with slip stitch, but twist the chain once before joining (Mobius twist).
**Round 1:** Chain 2 (counts as first hdc), hdc in each chain around, join. (100 hdc)
**Rounds 2-8:** Chain 2, hdc in each stitch around, join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Make sure the chain is twisted exactly once before joining.
A chunkier yarn gives a cozier scarf.
commonMistakes: Twisting the chain more than once or not at all.
Forgetting to place a stitch marker at the start.

name: Sunburst Granny Square
shortDescription: A colorful sunburst granny square with a textured center. Great for blankets, bags, and pillows.

difficulty.reasoning: Introduces cluster stitches and color changes. Slightly more complex than a basic granny.

yarn.notes: Use 3 colors for the sunburst effect.

gauge.notes: Make a test square to check.

instructions: **Round 1 (Color A):** Magic ring, chain 3, 11 dc in ring, join. (12 dc). Fasten off.
**Round 2 (Color B):** Join new color in any dc. Chain 3, dc in same stitch. 2 dc in each stitch around, join. (24 dc). Fasten off.
**Round 3 (Color C):** Join in any stitch. (Sc, hdc, dc) in same stitch, skip 1 — repeat around, join.

**Round 4 (Color C):** Slip stitch in next 2 stitches to reach a hdc. Chain 3 (counts as dc), dc in same stitch (increase), *dc in next 8 stitches, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in next stitch (corner); repeat from * 3 more times, dc in next 8 stitches, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in last stitch, join to top of ch-3.
beginnerTips: Use highly contrasting colors for a dramatic sunburst effect.
Block all squares to the same size before joining.
commonMistakes: Not changing colors tightly — leave room for the next round.
Uneven tension making the square lopsided.

name: Solid Hexagon
shortDescription: A solid hexagon motif using double crochet. Great for blankets, rugs, and joining into creative shapes.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple 6-sided increases using dc clusters. Very repetitive once established.

yarn.notes: Great for scraps.

instructions: **Round 1:** Magic ring, chain 3 (counts as dc), 11 dc in ring, join. (12 dc)
**Round 2:** Chain 4 (counts as dc + ch 1), *dc in next stitch, chain 1; repeat from * around, join in 3rd ch of starting chain 4. (12 dc, 12 ch-1 sps)

**Round 3:** Slip stitch to first ch-1 space. Chain 3 (counts as dc), (dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in same space — first corner. *2 dc in next ch-1 space, (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in next ch-1 space (corner); repeat from * around, ending with 2 dc in last ch-1 space, join. (6 corners)
**Round 4:** Slip stitch to corner space. Chain 3, (dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in same space. *Dc in each stitch across to next corner (4 dc), (2 dc, ch 2, 2 dc) in corner space; repeat from * around, join.
**Round 5:** Repeat Round 4 — each side gains 4 more dc. Continue until hexagon reaches desired size.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Each round adds 2 dc per side — it grows fast!
Join hexagons at the corners for unique patterns.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the ch 2 at each corner.
Losing count of dc on the sides.

name: Diagonal Waffle Cloth
shortDescription: A dishcloth with a diagonal waffle texture using front post double crochet. Absorbent and scrubby.

difficulty.reasoning: Introduces front post double crochet (FPdc) — the waffle texture.

yarn.notes: Must use 100% cotton for dishcloths!

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 24.
**Row 1:** Dc in 4th chain from hook and each across. (22 dc)
**Row 2:** Chain 3, turn. FPdc around next dc, dc in next — repeat across, ending with dc in top of turning chain.
**Row 3:** Chain 3, turn. Dc in next, FPdc around next — alternate across, ending with dc.
**Rows 4-18:** Repeat Rows 2 and 3 (waffle pattern).
**Border:** Sc evenly around the edges, working 3 sc in corners.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Only use cotton — acrylic is unsafe and doesn't absorb well.
The waffle texture gets softer with each wash.
commonMistakes: Confusing FPdc with regular dc — FPdc goes around the post, not through the top.
Using non-cotton yarn.

name: Spiral Rope Coaster
shortDescription: A thick, absorbent coaster made from cotton rope. Works up fast and protects surfaces from moisture.

difficulty.reasoning: Continuous spiral in the round using only single crochet. No joining needed.

yarn.notes: Use 100% cotton for absorbency.

instructions: **Round 1:** Magic ring, 6 sc in ring. Do not join — work in a continuous spiral.
**Round 2:** 2 sc in each stitch around. (12 sc)
**Round 3:** (Sc in next, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (18 sc)
**Round 4:** (Sc in next 2, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (24 sc)
**Round 5:** (Sc in next 3, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (30 sc)
**Round 6:** Sc in each stitch around. (30 sc)
**Finishing:** Slip stitch to next stitch, fasten off. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Place a stitch marker in the first stitch to track rounds.
Use a tighter tension so the coaster lies flat.
commonMistakes: The coaster curling into a bowl — add more increases or block it flat.
Losing count of rounds without a marker.

name: Simple Cowl
shortDescription: A cozy infinity-style cowl worked in the round. Uses only double crochet and works up in an evening.

difficulty.reasoning: Worked in the round with simple double crochet. No seaming needed.

yarn.notes: A soft, warm yarn is ideal.

hook.notes: Slightly larger hook gives nice drape.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 80 (or any multiple of 2). Join with slip stitch to form a ring, being careful not to twist.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), double crochet in each chain around, join. (80 dc)
**Rounds 2-8:** Chain 3, double crochet in each stitch around, join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Make sure the chain isn't twisted before joining.
Add more rounds for a taller cowl.
commonMistakes: Twisting the foundation chain when joining.
Skipping the joining slip stitch.

name: Messy Bun Beanie
shortDescription: A trendy beanie with a hole at the crown for ponytails or buns. Quick to make and perfect for gifting.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple construction with basic stitches and increases.

instructions: **Round 1:** Make a magic ring. Chain 1, work 10 double crochet into the ring, join. (10 dc)
**Round 2:** Chain 1, 2 double crochet in each stitch around, join. (20 dc)
**Round 3:** Chain 1, *double crochet in next stitch, 2 dc in next*, repeat around, join. (30 dc)
**Rounds 4-12:** Chain 1, double crochet in each stitch around, join.
**Finishing:** Chain 1, slip stitch in next 8 stitches to create a small brim fold. Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track the start of each round.
Keep tension consistent for an even brim.
commonMistakes: Not marking the start of the round.
Tightening the magic ring too much.

name: Corner to Corner Baby Blanket
shortDescription: A modern baby blanket worked diagonally from corner to corner. Uses only double crochet and chain stitches.

difficulty.reasoning: C2C technique requires counting and following a diagonal pattern.

instructions: **Row 1 (Increase):** Chain 6. Double crochet in 4th chain from hook and in next 2 chains. This makes the first block.
**Row 2 (Increase):** Chain 6. Double crochet in 4th chain from hook and in next 2 chains. Slip stitch to the chain-3 space of previous row, chain 3, work 3 dc in same space.
**Rows 3-20 (Increase):** Continue increasing. Chain 6 at start of each new row. Work 3 dc blocks in each chain-3 space across, increasing by one block each row.
**Rows 21-40 (Decrease):** Slip stitch across first block to start the row. Chain 3, work 3 dc in next chain-3 space across. Decrease by one block each row until one block remains.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Add a single crochet border around the entire blanket if desired.
beginnerTips: Use a different color for every 5 rows to track your progress.
Count your blocks after every row to catch mistakes early.
commonMistakes: Not counting blocks before starting the decrease section.
Skipping the chain-6 at the start of increase rows.

name: Simple Lace Triangle Shawl
shortDescription: An airy triangular shawl with an easy-to-memorize lace repeat. A great introduction to lace crochet.

difficulty.reasoning: Lace pattern requires counting stitches and repeating rows.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 4. Work 3 double crochet in 4th chain from hook (this forms the center point). Chain 2, 4 double crochet in same stitch. Turn.

**Row 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc). Work 3 dc in first stitch. (Chain 1, skip 1, dc in next stitch) across to center. Chain 2 at center point, dc in same stitch. Repeat (dc, ch 1, skip 1) across. Work 4 dc in last stitch. Turn.
**Row 2:** Chain 3, 3 dc in first stitch. (Chain 2, sc in next ch-1 space) across to center. Chain 2 at center. Repeat (sc in next ch-1 space, ch 2) across. 4 dc in last stitch. Turn.
**Row 3:** Chain 3, 3 dc in first stitch. (Chain 3, sc in next ch-2 space) across to center. Chain 3 at center. Repeat (sc in ch-2 space, ch 3) across. 4 dc in last stitch. Turn.
**Repeat:** Continue rows 1-3, increasing the lace pattern by one repeat on each side every row. Work until shawl reaches desired size.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Block gently to open up the lace pattern.
beginnerTips: Blocking is key for lace — it opens up the stitches beautifully.
Use stitch markers at the center chain-2 space to avoid losing your place.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the chain-2 increase at the center.
Not blocking the finished shawl to see the lace pattern.

name: Granny Square Tote Bag
shortDescription: A boho-style tote made from granny squares. A great way to use up scrap yarn in multiple colors.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires making multiple granny squares and seaming them together.

instructions: **Make 10 Granny Squares (follow standard granny square pattern):** Round 1: Chain 4, join with slip stitch to form ring. Chain 3, 2 dc in ring, (ch 2, 3 dc in ring) 3 times, ch 2, join. Round 2: Slip stitch to corner, ch 3, (2 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in corner, *ch 1, (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in next corner*, repeat around, join. Rounds 3-4: Continue, adding (3 dc, ch 1) along sides and (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in corners.
**Seaming:** Arrange squares in a 2x5 rectangle. Using tapestry needle and matching yarn, whip stitch squares together through back loops only.
**Fold:** Fold rectangle in half widthwise so the 2-square ends overlap. Sew side seams.
**Handles:** Attach yarn at top edge. Chain 80, slip stitch back to starting point. Double crochet evenly along the chain for a sturdy handle. Repeat on the other side.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends. Optionally sew in a fabric lining and add a magnetic snap closure.
beginnerTips: Block all squares to the same size before seaming for a professional look.
Weave in ends as you go to save time at the end.
commonMistakes: Squares not matching size, making seaming difficult.
Twisting the handles when attaching them.

name: Tiny Amigurumi Cat
shortDescription: A cute miniature cat that works up quickly. Learn amigurumi basics: magic ring, increases, and invisible decreases.

difficulty.reasoning: Small project with simple shapes, but requires careful counting for amigurumi.

instructions: **Head:** Make a magic ring. Round 1: 6 sc in ring. (6) Round 2: 2 sc in each stitch. (12) Round 3: (sc in next, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (18) Rounds 4-6: sc in each stitch. (18) Round 7: (sc in next, sc2tog) repeat around. (12) Stuff firmly. Round 8: sc2tog around. (6) Fasten off, weave closed.

**Body:** Make a magic ring. Round 1: 6 sc in ring. (6) Round 2: 2 sc in each stitch. (12) Round 3: (sc in next, 2 sc in next) repeat around. (18) Rounds 4-5: sc in each stitch. (18) Round 6: (sc in next, sc2tog) repeat around. (12) Stuff. Round 7: sc2tog around. (6) Fasten off, leaving a tail for sewing.
**Ears (make 2):** Chain 4. Sc in 2nd chain from hook, hdc in next, dc in last. Fasten off, leaving tail.
**Tail:** Chain 10. Sc in 2nd chain from hook and across. Fasten off, leaving tail.
**Assembly:** Sew head to body. Attach ears to top of head. Sew tail to back. Embroider eyes, nose, and whiskers with black thread.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track rounds — it's easy to lose count in amigurumi.
Stuff firmly but not too tight; the toy should be squishable.
commonMistakes: Losing count of stitches between rounds.
Overstuffing, which causes the fabric to stretch and show stuffing.

name: Macrame-Inspired Coaster Set
shortDescription: A set of four cotton coasters with a knotted macrame look. Made with front post stitches and simple color blocks.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses post stitches but the pattern is repetitive and easy to memorize.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 6, join with slip stitch to form ring.
**Round 1:** Chain 1, work 12 single crochet into ring, join. (12 sc)
**Round 2:** Chain 2, double crochet in same stitch. 2 dc in each stitch around, join. (24 dc)
**Round 3:** Chain 2, *FPdc around next stitch, dc in next* repeat around, join. (12 FPdc, 12 dc)
**Round 4:** Chain 2, *dc in next, FPdc around next* repeat around, join. (12 dc, 12 FPdc)
**Round 5:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around, join. Fasten off and weave in ends.
**Repeat:** Make 4 identical coasters.
beginnerTips: Front post stitches create the woven macrame effect — practice on a swatch first.
Cotton yarn is best for coasters as it's absorbent and heat-tolerant.
commonMistakes: Confusing FPdc (front post) with regular dc placement.
Skipping the slip stitch join at the end of each round.

name: Twisted Headband Ear Warmer
shortDescription: A stylish twisted headband that doubles as an ear warmer. One piece construction with a sewn twist for a modern look.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple rectangle with a sewn twist. No shaping required.

instructions: **Rectangle:** Chain 13. Half double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and across. (11 hdc)
**Rows 2-30:** Chain 2 (counts as hdc), skip first stitch, hdc in each stitch across. (11 hdc)
**Finishing Row:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch across. Fasten off leaving a long tail.
**Twist:** Fold the rectangle in half so the short ends meet. Twist the center once, then sew the short ends together using the long tail.
**Final:** Weave in any remaining ends. The headband naturally curves to fit the head.
beginnerTips: Use soft, non-itchy yarn since this sits against the forehead.
The twist naturally creates the fit — adjust the tightness by sewing the seam slightly tighter or looser.
commonMistakes: Using scratchy yarn that irritates the forehead.
Not leaving a long enough tail for seaming the twist.

name: Infinity Scarf Loop
shortDescription: A seamless infinity scarf worked in the round. Creates a cozy, wearable loop with no ends to seam.

difficulty.reasoning: Worked in the round with simple stitches. No seaming required.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 80, being careful not to twist. Join with slip stitch to form a ring.
**Round 1:** Chain 1, single crochet in each chain around, join. (80 sc)
**Round 2:** Chain 2 (counts as hdc), half double crochet in each stitch around, join. (80 hdc)
**Rounds 3-8:** Repeat Round 2.
**Round 9:** Chain 1, reverse single crochet (crab stitch) in each stitch around for a decorative edge. Fasten off.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block lightly if desired.
beginnerTips: Make sure the foundation chain isn't twisted before joining — this is the most common mistake!
Use a stitch marker to mark the start of each round.
commonMistakes: Twisting the chain when joining to form the loop.
Tight tension making the scarf too stiff.

name: Linen Stitch Market Bag
shortDescription: A sturdy, eco-friendly market bag made with the linen stitch. Expands to hold groceries and folds flat when not in use.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple repeat of chain and single crochet. Easy to memorize.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 26. Round 1: Sc in 2nd chain from hook and across. Work on other side of chain: sc in each chain across, join. (50 sc)
**Rounds 2-5:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around, join. This forms the flat base.
**Round 6 (Linen Stitch start):** Chain 1, *sc in next, ch 1, skip 1* repeat around, join. (25 sc, 25 ch-1 spaces)
**Rounds 7-16:** Chain 1, *sc in next ch-1 space, ch 1, skip next sc* repeat around, join.
**Handles:** Find the center 10 stitches on each side. Mark them. Round 17: Linen stitch as established, but chain 20 over the marked stitches to create handle openings.
**Round 18:** Sc in each stitch and chain around, working 20 sc into each handle chain. (60 sc)
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Cotton yarn is ideal — it's strong and machine washable.
The linen stitch creates a dense fabric that holds its shape well.
commonMistakes: Losing count of the linen stitch pattern (sc in space, ch 1, skip).
Making handles too short to fit over the shoulder.

name: Baby Rattle Ball
shortDescription: A soft, safe baby rattle made with a crochet ball and a hidden jingle bell inside. Machine washable and baby-safe.

difficulty.reasoning: Simple sphere construction with increases and decreases.

instructions: **Ball:** Make a magic ring. Round 1: 6 sc in ring. (6) Round 2: 2 sc in each stitch. (12) Round 3: (sc in next, 2 sc in next) repeat. (18) Rounds 4-7: sc in each stitch. (18) Insert jingle bell inside, stuff around it. Round 8: (sc in next, sc2tog) repeat. (12) Round 9: sc2tog around. (6) Fasten off, weave closed.
**Stripe detail (optional):** Before closing completely, add a round in a contrasting color for visual interest.
**Safety check:** Ensure the bell is fully encased and no stuffing is poking through. Give it a gentle squeeze test.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends securely. Wash gently before giving to baby.
beginnerTips: Use a baby-safe jingle bell that won't rust or break apart.
Make sure no stitches are loose enough for small fingers to pull stuffing out.
commonMistakes: Using a bell that's too large or has sharp edges.
Not stuffing enough around the bell, leaving it loose inside.

name: Lace Wrist Warmers
shortDescription: Delicate fingerless mitts using sport-weight yarn. A quick, elegant project that's perfect for cooler mornings.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses double crochet and chain-spacing for a lacy look; requires consistent tension and stitch counting.

yarn.notes: A smooth sport-weight yarn gives the best stitch definition.

hook.notes: Use the smaller end if using an ergonomic hook.

instructions: **Foundation Chain:** Chain 28, slip stitch to form a ring, being careful not to twist.
**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), double crochet in next chain and each around, slip stitch to top of chain-3. (28 dc)
**Round 2-6:** Chain 3, double crochet in each stitch around, slip stitch to join. (28 dc each round)
**Thumb Opening Round 7:** Chain 3, double crochet in next 5 stitches, chain 4, skip 4 stitches, double crochet in remaining 18 stitches, slip stitch to join.
**Round 8-10:** Chain 3, double crochet in each stitch and in each chain of the thumb opening, slip stitch to join. (28 dc)
**Edging:** Chain 1, single crochet in each stitch around, slip stitch to join. Fasten off. Repeat for second wrist warmer.
beginnerTips: Mark the first stitch of each round so you don't lose your place.
Count your stitches after the thumb opening round.
commonMistakes: Twisting the foundation chain when joining.
Making the thumb opening too tight—chain loosely.

name: Sport-Weight Baby Booties
shortDescription: Adorable newborn booties using fine sport-weight yarn. Makes a wonderful baby shower gift.

difficulty.reasoning: Includes increases, decreases, and seaming; requires attention to shaping.

yarn.notes: Soft, washable yarn is best for baby items.

hook.notes: A smaller hook creates a denser fabric for booties.

instructions: **Sole:** Chain 8. Single crochet in 2nd chain from hook and next 5 chains, 3 sc in last chain. Working on opposite side, sc in next 5 chains, 2 sc in last chain. (16 sc)
**Sole Round 2:** Sc in each stitch around, increasing 1 stitch at each end (18 sc).
**Sole Round 3:** Sc in each stitch around, increasing 1 stitch at each end (20 sc). Fasten off.
**Upper:** Join yarn in center back of sole. Sc in each stitch around for 5 rounds working in back loops only.
**Toe Decrease:** Fold bootie flat. Sc decrease across the toe section 3 times, sc to end. (17 sc)

**Cuff:** Chain 6, sc in 2nd chain from hook and next 4 chains. Slip stitch into next stitch of bootie. Turn, sc in back loop of each cuff stitch. Repeat around for 3 rounds. Fasten off, sew button to cuff if desired.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to keep track of rounds.
Weave in ends as you go to save time later.
commonMistakes: Using the wrong loop (work in back loops only for the upper).
Skipping the gauge swatch—booties need to fit.

name: DK Triangle Shawl
shortDescription: A classic top-down triangle shawl using DK weight yarn. Lightweight and perfect for spring evenings.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses increases, double crochet, and chain-space patterns; requires counting and pattern repetition.

yarn.notes: A soft drapey yarn works best for shawls.

hook.notes: A slightly larger hook gives better drape.

gauge.notes: Gauge affects final size and drape.

instructions: **Center Top:** Chain 4, double crochet in 4th chain from hook. (2 dc)
**Row 1:** Chain 4 (counts as dc + ch1), dc in same stitch, chain 1, dc in same stitch. (4 dc, 2 ch-1 spaces)
**Row 2:** Chain 4, (dc, ch1, dc) in first ch-1 space, ch1, (dc, ch1, dc) in next ch-1 space, dc in top of chain-3. (6 dc, 4 ch-1 spaces)
**Row 3:** Chain 4, dc in first space. *(dc, ch1, dc) in next ch-1 space* repeat across, ending with dc in last space and dc in top of chain-3.
**Repeat Row 3:** Continue until shawl reaches desired size (about 24-30 rows).
**Edging:** Single crochet evenly around all edges, working 3 sc in each corner. Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use stitch markers on the first and last stitch of each row.
Block the finished shawl to open up the lace pattern.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the chain-1 between increases.
Uneven edges—make sure to dc in the top of the turning chain.

name: Lightweight Pullover Sweater
shortDescription: A beginner-friendly crochet sweater made from two simple rectangles seamed together. DK weight keeps it lightweight.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires seaming, gauge matching, and understanding of garment construction.

yarn.notes: Choose a yarn with good drape for a flattering fit.

hook.notes: Using a slightly larger hook than recommended gives better drape.

gauge.notes: Gauge is critical for correct sizing.

instructions: **Back Panel:** Chain 60 (adjust for your size). Double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (58 dc)
**Work Even:** Chain 3, turn. Double crochet in each stitch across. Repeat for 40 rows or until panel reaches underarm.
**Shoulder Decrease:** Chain 3, dc across first 20 stitches. Fasten off. Skip center 18 stitches, join yarn in next stitch, chain 3, dc across last 20 stitches. Fasten off.
**Front Panel:** Repeat same as back until 30 rows. For neck opening: work 20 dc, chain 18 (skip center 18 stitches for neck), dc across last 20 stitches. Continue for 10 more rows.
**Seaming:** With right sides together, sew shoulder seams and side seams using the mattress stitch or whip stitch.
**Sleeves:** Optional: pick up stitches around armholes and work in rounds of double crochet for desired sleeve length. Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Make a gauge swatch and measure it before starting.
Try on the panels as you go to check sizing.
commonMistakes: Wrong gauge leading to incorrect size.
Sewing seams too tightly, restricting movement.

name: Crochet Market Tote
shortDescription: A sturdy market bag using DK cotton yarn. The mesh pattern stretches to hold groceries while being compact when folded.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses mesh stitch pattern and working in the round; requires attention to the repeat.

yarn.notes: Cotton gives the bag structure and durability.

hook.notes: A slightly larger hook creates a more open mesh.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for this bag.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 36, slip stitch to join. Chain 1, sc in each chain around. (36 sc)
**Round 1:** Chain 4 (counts as dc + ch1), skip 1 stitch, dc in next. Repeat around, slip stitch to 3rd chain of ch-4. (18 dc, 18 ch-1 spaces)
**Round 2:** Chain 4, dc in next dc. Repeat around, slip stitch to join. Continue this mesh pattern for 20 rounds.
**Top Band:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch and chain space around for 3 rounds. (36 sc each round)

**Handles:** Chain 50, skip 12 sc, slip stitch in next sc. Sc in each chain and sc around. Chain 50, skip remaining 12 sc, slip stitch to first sc. Sc in each chain and sc around. Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track the start of each round.
Cotton yarn has less stretch—make handles generously long.
commonMistakes: Twisting the base chain when joining.
Making handles too short to go over the shoulder.

name: Striped Mug Cozy
shortDescription: A cheerful striped mug cozy in DK yarn. Quick to make and customizable with your favorite colors.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet and simple color changes. No shaping required.

yarn.notes: Cotton is best for heat resistance. Use small amounts of 2-3 colors.

hook.notes: Use the size recommended on your yarn label.

instructions: **Band:** Chain 9. Single crochet in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (8 sc)
**Row 2-30:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in back loop only of each stitch across. (8 sc) Change colors every 5 rows for stripes.
**Finishing:** Fold band around mug. Sew button on one end. Chain 6 at the other end for a button loop. Button loop should fit snugly around the button.
Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Use a button that matches one of your yarn colors.
Work a gauge swatch if you want a custom fit for a specific mug.
commonMistakes: Making the band too tight—it should wrap around with a slight overlap.
Forgetting to leave a button opening.

name: Cozy House Slippers
shortDescription: Warm, sturdy house slippers made with worsted weight yarn. The double-thick sole keeps your feet off cold floors.

difficulty.reasoning: Requires shaping, increasing, and decreasing for the heel and toe.

yarn.notes: A sturdy, washable yarn works best for slippers.

hook.notes: Use the recommended hook size for your yarn.

notions: Fabric glue or non-slip fabric paint (optional)

gauge.notes: Gauge is important for correct fit.

instructions: **Sole:** Chain 12. 2 hdc in 3rd chain from hook, hdc in next 9 chains, 5 hdc in last chain. Working on opposite side: hdc in next 9 chains, 3 hdc in last chain. Join with slip stitch. (28 hdc)
**Sole Round 2:** Chain 2, hdc in same stitch, 2 hdc in next stitch, hdc in next 9 stitches, (2 hdc in next)*5 times, hdc in next 9 stitches, (2 hdc in next)*3 times. Join. (38 hdc)
**Sides:** Chain 2, hdc in back loop only of each stitch around. Join. (38 hdc)
**Sides Round 2-5:** Chain 2, hdc in each stitch around. Join. (38 hdc each round)
**Heel:** Chain 2, hdc in next 10 stitches. Turn. Hdc decrease, hdc in next 6, hdc decrease. Turn. Repeat decrease row 3 times. Fasten off.
**Cuff:** Join yarn at heel. Chain 2, hdc around the top opening for 4 rounds. Fasten off. Repeat for second slipper.
beginnerTips: Use stitch markers to count increases on the sole.
Test fit as you go—adjust length by adding or removing chains on the sole.
commonMistakes: Making the sole too flat—the increase rounds are important for the foot shape.
Forgetting to work in back loops only for the side walls.

name: Simple Beginner Poncho
shortDescription: A cozy poncho made from two large rectangles sewn together. Extremely beginner-friendly and forgiving of gauge.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only double crochet and simple seaming. No shaping or increases.

yarn.notes: A soft, drapey worsted weight yarn works great.

hook.notes: A larger hook gives the poncho better drape.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for this garment.

instructions: **Panel 1 (Front):** Chain 50. Double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (48 dc)
**Row 2:** Chain 3, turn. Dc in each stitch across. Repeat for 40 rows or until panel measures about 20 inches.
**Panel 2 (Back):** Repeat the same as Panel 1.
**Seaming:** Fold each panel in half. Sew the top edge of each panel together, leaving an 8-inch opening in the center for the neck.
**Neck Edging:** Join yarn at neck edge. Single crochet evenly around the neck opening. Fasten off.
**Fringe (optional):** Cut 10-inch yarn strands. Fold each in half, pull through bottom edge stitches, and pull ends through loop. Space fringe every 2 stitches around the bottom. Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Block both panels before seaming for a professional look.
Try the poncho on before adding fringe to check the length.
commonMistakes: Making the neck opening too small—measure your head circumference.
Uneven panels—count rows carefully.

name: Rope Storage Basket
shortDescription: A sturdy storage basket made by crocheting with t-shirt yarn or triple-strand worsted weight. Perfect for organizing shelves.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet worked in a spiral; requires consistent tension for straight sides.

yarn.notes: For a sturdier basket, hold 2-3 strands of worsted weight together.

hook.notes: Use a larger hook if holding multiple strands.

gauge.notes: Gauge affects stiffness—tighter is better for baskets.

instructions: **Base:** Make a magic ring. Round 1: 6 sc in ring. (6 sc)
**Round 2:** 2 sc in each stitch around. (12 sc)
**Round 3:** *Sc in next stitch, 2 sc in next* repeat around. (18 sc)
**Round 4:** *Sc in next 2 stitches, 2 sc in next* repeat around. (24 sc)
**Round 5-7:** Continue increasing 6 stitches each round until base is desired diameter (about 6-7 rounds total).
**Sides:** Sc in back loop only of each stitch around for 8 rounds. Switch to both loops for 4 more rounds.
**Edging:** Slip stitch in each stitch around. Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track rounds when working in a spiral.
Hold two strands together for a sturdier basket.
commonMistakes: Crocheting too loosely—tight tension gives the basket structure.
Not increasing enough on the base—it should lie flat.

name: Thick Cotton Potholder
shortDescription: A double-thick potholder using cotton yarn. The thermal stitch creates an insulating layer for kitchen safety.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked through the back loop. No shaping.

yarn.notes: Use 100% cotton—acrylic will melt with heat!

hook.notes: Use the size recommended on the yarn.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 26.
**Row 1:** Single crochet in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (25 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in back loop only of each stitch across. (25 sc)
**Rows 3-24:** Repeat Row 2. The fabric will be double-thick and dense.
**Hanging Loop:** Chain 12, slip stitch to the corner of the potholder. Sc in each chain back. Fasten off.
**Finishing:** Fold a second matching potholder (make two total). Sc around the edges to join them, working 3 sc in corners for a neat finish. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Cotton is mandatory—never use acrylic for potholders.
Work tightly for better insulation.
commonMistakes: Using acrylic yarn that can melt.
Crocheting too loosely—the potholder should be dense.

name: Quick Velvet Scrunchies
shortDescription: Luxurious velvet scrunchies that work up in minutes. Great for using small amounts of specialty yarn.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked around a hair elastic. Straightforward and fast.

yarn.notes: Velvet or soft acrylic gives the best look. Use scraps.

hook.notes: A smaller hook makes denser scrunchies.

instructions: **Setup:** Hold hair elastic with your fingers. Insert hook through the elastic, yarn over and pull up a loop.
**Round 1:** Single crochet around the elastic, covering it completely. Work about 30-40 sc depending on your tension.
**Round 2:** Slip stitch to join. Chain 1, 2 sc in each stitch around. (60-80 sc)
**Round 3:** Sc in each stitch around. Fasten off, leaving a long tail.
**Finishing:** Sew the ends together neatly using the yarn tail. Weave in all ends. Fluff the scrunchie.
beginnerTips: Use a tapestry needle to sew the ends together invisibly.
Experiment with different yarn textures for different looks.
commonMistakes: Crocheting too tightly around the elastic—it should stretch.
Not covering the elastic completely in the first round.

name: Bulky Beanies
shortDescription: A quick-to-make beanie using bulky yarn. Works up in under an hour for instant gratification.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses half double crochet in the round with simple decreases at the crown.

yarn.notes: A single skein of bulky yarn is usually enough.

hook.notes: Use a larger hook for a looser fabric.

instructions: **Magic Ring:** Make a magic ring, chain 2 (does not count as stitch).
**Round 1:** 8 hdc in ring, pull tight, join with slip stitch. (8 hdc)
**Round 2:** Chain 2, 2 hdc in each stitch around, join. (16 hdc)
**Round 3:** Chain 2, *hdc in next stitch, 2 hdc in next* repeat around, join. (24 hdc)
**Round 4:** Chain 2, *hdc in next 2 stitches, 2 hdc in next* repeat around, join. (32 hdc)
**Round 5-10:** Chain 2, hdc in each stitch around, join. (32 hdc each round)
**Ribbed Brim:** Chain 1, sc in back loop only of each stitch for 3 rounds. Fasten off. Weave in ends. Add pom-pom if desired.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track the first stitch of each round.
Try the beanie on as you go to check the fit.
commonMistakes: Increasing too much—the crown should lie flat, not ruffle.
Making the hat too tall—bulky yarn stacks up fast.

name: Bulky Cowl Neck Warmer
shortDescription: A stylish infinity cowl worked in bulky yarn. The half double crochet creates a warm, dense fabric perfect for winter.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only half double crochet worked in joined rounds. No increases or decreases.

yarn.notes: One to two skeins of bulky yarn, depending on desired length.

hook.notes: A larger hook keeps the fabric from being too stiff.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for this project.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 26, slip stitch to join, being careful not to twist.
**Round 1:** Chain 2 (does not count as hdc). Hdc in each chain around, slip stitch to first hdc. (26 hdc)
**Round 2-15:** Chain 2, hdc in each stitch around, slip stitch to join. Repeat until cowl reaches desired width (about 10-12 inches).
**Finishing:** Fasten off and weave in ends. Block gently if desired.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to mark the first stitch of each round.
Block the cowl lightly to even out the stitches.
commonMistakes: Twisting the foundation chain when joining—lay it flat first.
Crocheting too tightly—bulky yarn needs a relaxed tension.

name: Chunky Throw Pillow
shortDescription: A super-chunky throw pillow cover using bulky yarn. The simple rectangle folds into a pillow cover with an envelope back.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only double crochet worked as a rectangle. No shaping or seaming.

yarn.notes: Bulky chenille or chunky acrylic gives a soft, plush feel.

hook.notes: A larger hook creates a softer, drapier fabric.

instructions: **Main Panel:** Chain 26. Double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (24 dc)
**Rows 2-20:** Chain 3, turn. Dc in each stitch across. (24 dc each row)
**Fold and Seam:** Fold the rectangle in half. Whip stitch the bottom and one side closed.
**Envelope Back:** For a removable cover: crochet a second rectangle of the same size. Attach along the bottom edge only. Add button loops along the open side.
**Finishing:** Insert pillow form. If using buttons, sew them opposite the button loops. Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your pillow form and adjust the chain length as needed.
Block the panel before seaming for a professional finish.
commonMistakes: Making the panel too small—measure against the pillow form.
Using a hook that's too small, making stiff fabric that doesn't drape.

name: Super Bulky Arm Knit Blanket
shortDescription: A luxurious hand-crocheted blanket using super bulky yarn. Works up incredibly fast—perfect for last-minute gifts.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet with giant yarn. The technique is simple but requires arm strength.

yarn.notes: Use jumbo or super bulky yarn. You can also hold 3-4 strands of bulky together.

hook.notes: Use a giant hook (15mm or larger). Or crochet with your hands!

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for a blanket.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 40 (or any width desired).
**Row 1:** Single crochet in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (39 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in each stitch across. (39 sc)
**Rows 3-20:** Repeat Row 2 until the blanket reaches desired length (about 20-25 rows for a throw).
**Border:** Single crochet evenly around all edges, working 3 sc in each corner. Fasten off.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends with a large yarn needle. Block gently if needed.
beginnerTips: This project is heavy—support the weight as you work.
Count stitches every few rows since mistakes are visible in giant yarn.
commonMistakes: Using regular-weight yarn instead of super bulky—the look won't be the same.
Forgetting that this blanket is heavy when finished.

name: Jumbo Pet Bed
shortDescription: A plush, round pet bed using super bulky yarn. Your cat or small dog will love this cozy nest.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses half double crochet in the round with increases for the base. Requires consistent tension.

yarn.notes: Super bulky chenille gives a luxurious, plush feel.

instructions: **Base:** Make a magic ring. Round 1: 8 hdc in ring, join. (8 hdc)
**Round 2:** Chain 2, 2 hdc in each stitch around, join. (16 hdc)
**Round 3:** Chain 2, *hdc in next stitch, 2 hdc in next* around, join. (24 hdc)
**Rounds 4-8:** Continue increasing 8 stitches each round until base is desired diameter (about 16-18 inches for a cat bed).
**Walls (no increase):** Chain 2, hdc in back loop only of each stitch around for 8 rounds. This creates the side walls.
**Edging:** Slip stitch around the top edge. Fasten off. Insert a cushion or stuffing. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to track your rounds.
Test the bed size by having your pet sit on it midway.
commonMistakes: Increasing too fast—the base should lie flat without ruffling.
Making the walls too tall—pets prefer low walls they can climb over.

name: Cozy Leg Warmers
shortDescription: Leg warmers worked flat and seamed. Customize the length and add a fold-over cuff for extra warmth.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses double crochet worked flat with simple seaming. Straightforward construction.

yarn.notes: A wool blend adds warmth and elasticity.

hook.notes: Use the recommended size for your yarn.

instructions: **Cuff:** Chain 20. Double crochet in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (18 dc)
**Row 2-6:** Chain 3, turn. Dc in each stitch across. (18 dc each row)
**Fold Cuff:** Fold the cuff in half lengthwise and seam the short edges together to form a ring. Set aside.
**Leg Panel:** Chain 16. Dc in 3rd chain from hook and each across. (14 dc)
**Rows 2-20:** Chain 3, turn. Dc in each stitch across. Continue until panel measures about 14 inches.
**Assembly:** Seam the long edges of the leg panel together. Attach the cuff to the bottom. Repeat for second leg warmer. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Try on the leg warmer as you work to check the fit.
Add an edging of single crochet for a cleaner finish.
commonMistakes: Making the leg too wide—it should fit snugly without bagging.
Forgetting to make the second one the same size.

name: Crochet Christmas Ornaments
shortDescription: Set of mini crochet ornaments: a star, a heart, and a mini stocking. Great for using scrap yarn and making gifts.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses small-scale work with increases, decreases, and shaping in the round.

yarn.notes: Use small amounts of red, green, white, and gold yarn.

hook.notes: A smaller hook gives tighter stitches for ornaments.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not relevant for ornaments.

instructions: **Star (make 2):** Chain 2. 5 sc in 2nd chain from hook. (5 sc)
**Star Points:** Chain 4, sl st in 2nd chain from hook, sc in next, hdc in last. Sl st to next sc on the base. Repeat 4 more times to make 5 points. Fasten off.
**Heart:** Magic ring, ch 2, 2 dc, ch 2, sl st, ch 2, 2 dc, hdc — all in ring. Pull tight to form heart shape. Fasten off.
**Mini Stocking:** Chain 6. Sc in 2nd chain from hook and next 3, 3 sc in last. Continue on opposite side: sc in 4 chains, 2 sc in last. Join. (14 sc)
Work 3 rounds sc evenly. For the heel: sc decrease, sc in 3, sc decrease. For the cuff: ch 4, sc in 2nd chain and next 2, slip stitch to stocking. Fasten off.
**Assembly:** Attach ribbon or ornament hook to each piece. Block lightly. (Optional: dip in diluted glue to stiffen.)
beginnerTips: Use a smaller hook than recommended for tightly stuffed ornaments.
Block the star pieces before sewing them together.
commonMistakes: Ornaments are too loose—use a smaller hook for tighter stitches.
Skipping the stiffening step—they'll hold shape better with glue.

name: Crochet Hoop Earrings
shortDescription: Lightweight, modern hoop earrings made with fine thread and wire hoops. An advanced beginner project that looks impressive.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses fine thread and small hoops; requires dexterity and precise tension.

yarn.notes: Use size 10 or 20 crochet thread for best results.

hook.notes: A steel hook in size 7 or 8 works with crochet thread.

instructions: **Setup:** Attach thread to the hoop earring finding with a slip knot around the hoop.
**Round 1:** Single crochet evenly around the hoop, covering the metal completely. Work about 30 sc for a 1.5-inch hoop.
**Round 2:** *Chain 3, skip 1 sc, slip stitch in next sc* repeat around the hoop.
**Round 3:** Slip stitch in each chain-3 space around to create a scalloped edge. Fasten off.
**Finishing:** Use jewelry pliers to close the hoop finding. Weave in the thread tail carefully. Repeat for second earring.
beginnerTips: Work in good lighting—fine thread is hard to see.
Use a thimble if your fingers get sore from the small hook.
commonMistakes: Using regular yarn instead of thread—it won't fit through the hoop.
Crocheting too loosely—the stitches should hug the hoop snugly.

name: Boho Plant Hanger with Beads
shortDescription: A macrame-style crochet plant hanger using worsted cotton. Wooden beads add a boho touch.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, slip stitches, and working with multiple strands; requires attention to the pattern repeat.

yarn.notes: Cotton is strong and holds the weight of a plant pot.

hook.notes: Use a slightly larger hook for a looser drape.

instructions: **Top Ring:** Chain 6, slip stitch to form a ring.
**Round 1:** Chain 10, sc into ring. Repeat 5 more times. (6 loops)
**Round 2:** Slip stitch into first loop, chain 12, sc into next loop. Repeat around. (6 longer loops)
**Bead Round:** String a bead onto yarn before making each loop. Chain 10 (with bead in middle), sc into next loop. Repeat around.
**Lower Section:** Chain 15, slip stitch into ring at bottom. Repeat to create 4-5 hanging strands. String beads onto the ends.
**Finishing:** Tie ends together in a knot at the bottom. Insert plant pot. Hang from the top ring.
beginnerTips: Thread beads onto the yarn BEFORE starting each section.
Test the hanger with your pot size before finishing.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to add beads before closing loops.
Making the hanger too short—the pot should sit inside comfortably.

name: Lacy Bookmark with Bead
shortDescription: An elegant lace bookmark using cotton thread. Makes a wonderful, thoughtful gift for book lovers.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses fine thread and lace stitches; requires counting and attention to the pattern.

yarn.notes: A fine cotton thread (sport weight) gives the best lace effect.

hook.notes: Use a smaller hook for tighter stitches.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 14.
**Row 1:** Double crochet in 6th chain from hook. *Chain 2, skip 2 chains, dc in next chain* repeat across. (4 dc, 3 ch-2 spaces)
**Row 2:** Chain 5 (counts as dc + ch2), dc in next dc. *Chain 2, dc in next dc* repeat across. End with dc in 3rd chain of ch-5.
**Rows 3-20:** Repeat Row 2 until bookmark measures about 8 inches.
**Top Loop:** Chain 12, slip stitch to first dc. Sc in each chain back. Fasten off.
**Bead:** Thread bead onto the top loop. Weave in all ends. Optional: dip in starch and block for a crisp finish.
beginnerTips: Use stitch markers to track the pattern repeat.
Blocking opens up the lace and makes it look professional.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the chain-2 between double crochets.
Skipping the last dc at the end of the row.

name: Textured Phone Pouch
shortDescription: A protective phone pouch with a textured stitch pattern. The flap keeps your phone secure.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single and double crochet in a simple textured pattern. No shaping.

yarn.notes: Cotton is durable and won't stretch out of shape.

hook.notes: Use the size recommended on your yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is important for correct phone fit.

instructions: **Pouch Body:** Chain 18 (adjust for your phone width).
**Row 1:** Sc in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (17 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in each stitch across.
**Row 3:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), turn. Dc in each stitch across.
**Rows 4-16:** Repeat rows 2-3 for texture pattern. End with a sc row.
**Flap:** Continue on the same piece: chain 1, sc in each stitch for 6 more rows. On the last row, chain 6 for a button loop, slip stitch to the edge.
**Assembly:** Fold the pouch body in half. Whip stitch the sides closed. Sew button onto the front of the pouch aligned with the button loop. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your phone before starting and adjust foundation chain.
Use contrasting thread to sew the button for a pop of color.
commonMistakes: Making the pouch too narrow—test with your phone.
Sewing the button in the wrong position.

name: Insulated Water Bottle Sling
shortDescription: A water bottle holder with an adjustable strap and drawstring top. The double-thick base insulates your drink.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses working in the round, increases for the base, and a drawstring closure.

yarn.notes: Cotton is sturdy and insulates well.

hook.notes: Use the recommended size for your yarn.

notions: Cord or ribbon for drawstring (24 inches)

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, slip stitch to form ring. Round 1: 6 sc in ring. (6 sc)
**Round 2:** 2 sc in each stitch around. (12 sc)
**Round 3:** *Sc in next stitch, 2 sc in next* around. (18 sc). Continue increasing until base matches your bottle diameter.
**Body:** Sc in back loop only of each stitch around for 12 rounds (or until the holder covers your bottle).
**Drawstring Holes:** Chain 3, skip 2 sc, dc in next stitch. Repeat around. Join with slip stitch.
**Drawstring:** Crochet a chain about 24 inches long. Weave through the holes. Add a strap: chain 60, attach to both sides of the holder. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Test your bottle size as you increase the base.
Use a plastic canvas circle inside the base for extra stability.
commonMistakes: Making the base too big—the bottle should fit snugly.
Drawstring holes not aligned—count stitches evenly.

name: Quilted Eyeglass Case
shortDescription: A padded eyeglass case with a quilted texture. The flap closure keeps glasses secure.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses the thermal stitch for a padded effect; requires even tension for the quilted look.

yarn.notes: Cotton gives the best structure for a case.

hook.notes: Use a slightly smaller hook for dense fabric.

gauge.notes: Gauge affects the snugness of the fit.

instructions: **Case Body:** Chain 20. Sc in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (19 sc)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in back loop only of each stitch across.
**Rows 3-16:** Repeat Row 2. The thermal stitch creates a thick, padded fabric.
**Flap:** Continue on the same piece: chain 1, sc in each stitch for 5 more rows.
**Button Loop:** Chain 8, slip stitch to the last sc of the flap. Sc in each chain back.
**Finishing:** Fold the body in half. Whip stitch the sides and bottom closed. Sew button to the front at the flap position. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker to count rows evenly on both sides.
Block the piece before seaming for a professional look.
commonMistakes: Making the case too flat—glasses need a bit of depth.
Sewing seams too tight, creating a lumpy edge.

name: Infinity Wristband
shortDescription: A braided-looking wristband made with a clever crochet technique. Adjustable to any wrist size.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses a simple 3-chain loop pattern that creates a braided effect.

yarn.notes: Use two contrasting colors for a braided look.

hook.notes: Use the size recommended for your yarn.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 8.
**Row 1:** Slip stitch in 2nd chain from hook. *Chain 3, skip 1 chain, slip stitch in next chain* repeat across. (3 loops)
**Row 2:** Chain 1, turn. Slip stitch in first chain-3 loop. *Chain 3, slip stitch in next chain-3 loop* repeat across.
**Rows 3-20:** Repeat Row 2 until the band measures about 7 inches (or your wrist size minus 1 inch for overlap).
**Button Loop End:** On the last row, chain 6 before the final slip stitch to create a button loop.
**Finishing:** Sew button or toggle to the opposite end. Weave in ends. Fasten around wrist.
beginnerTips: Use two colors, alternating every 2 rows for a striped braid effect.
Make the button loop slightly smaller than the button diameter.
commonMistakes: Making the band too loose—the braid stretches with wear.
Skipping the button loop—check before fastening off.

name: Mini Amigurumi Keychain
shortDescription: An adorable mini amigurumi animal keychain. Choose a bear, bunny, or cat face design.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses amigurumi techniques: magic ring, increases, decreases, and small parts assembly.

yarn.notes: Small amounts of main color plus scraps for ears and face.

hook.notes: Use a smaller hook than usual for tight stitches (prevents stuffing from showing).

notions: Safety eyes (6mm) or embroidery thread for face

instructions: **Head:** Magic ring, 6 sc in ring. (6 sc)
**Round 2:** 2 sc in each stitch around. (12 sc)
**Round 3:** *Sc in next stitch, 2 sc in next* around. (18 sc)
**Rounds 4-6:** Sc in each stitch around. (18 sc each round)
**Round 7:** *Sc in next stitch, sc2tog* around. (12 sc)
**Round 8:** Sc2tog around. (6 sc). Stuff firmly before closing. Fasten off, leave tail for sewing.
**Ears (make 2):** Magic ring, 4 sc. Round 2: 2 sc in each stitch. (8 sc). Fasten off, leave tails.
**Assembly:** Sew ears to top of head. Add safety eyes or embroider face. Attach key ring to top. Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Use safety eyes with locking washers for children's items.
Stuff firmly but don't overstuff—the shape should be round, not lumpy.
commonMistakes: Crocheting too loosely—use a smaller hook for amigurumi.
Forgetting to weave in ends securely—keychains get a lot of handling.
